Scanned: 11 modules across 1 package, 712 lines, 526 of them code.
43 public things to convert; none of them are registered with s0ma yet.
5 test files seen and left out of the numbers above.

Perimeter it would declare (`s0ma adopt init` writes this):
  source roots    src
  bootstrap files src/bookshelf/__main__.py
  package markers src/bookshelf/__init__.py
  mode            migration

Convert in this order, leaves first (10 modules):
  module                             size   proposed layer
  bookshelf.config                   medium DOMAIN (medium confidence)
  bookshelf.errors                   medium DOMAIN (medium confidence)
  bookshelf.models                   medium DOMAIN (high confidence)
  bookshelf.notifications            medium yours to choose
  bookshelf.storage                  medium INFRASTRUCTURE (low confidence)
  bookshelf.catalog                  small  yours to choose
  bookshelf.lending                  small  yours to choose
  bookshelf                          small  package marker — nothing to convert
  bookshelf.api                      medium PRESENTATION (low confidence)
  bookshelf.cli                      small  PRESENTATION (high confidence)
  Not in that list: src/bookshelf/__main__.py — declared above under `bootstrap_files`,
  so it stays plain Python; a s0ma project names its entry points.

Import cycles: none at load time. Every module can be converted after the ones it
  imports, which is what makes the order above a plan rather than a suggestion.

Worth knowing (1):
  ADOPT_SCAN_DEFERRED_CYCLE · bookshelf.catalog — `bookshelf.catalog` and
    `bookshelf.lending` refer to each other, and the only reason that is not a circle is
    that `bookshelf.catalog` does its import inside a function instead of at the top of
    the file. It has to stay that way: when you convert `bookshelf.catalog`, the import
    belongs under `deferred_requires:` and not under `requires:`. Moving it up — or
    letting a draft write it as an ordinary requirement — makes a circle the build will
    refuse.

Next: `s0ma adopt init` — it writes the perimeter above into pyproject.toml and touches
  no application file.
